headline: Analytics are still stale, but the market signal is clear: Real Dough's strongest lane is specific sourdough/Wisconsin credibility plus value proof while private label, cleaner national brands, and format-led frozen competitors get sharper.

items: Paid controls still look efficient in the trusted YTD export: Meta 'Straight From Wisconsin' has 13,622 link clicks at $0.11 CPC, and 'Meet Real Dough Pizza Co.' remains at 4.67% CTR with $0.11 CPC.

Founder/process content remains the most defensible organic signal: Founder Pro Tips is still the top Instagram engagement item, and ingredient reassurance now leads the Facebook reel backfill by average view time.
Demand capture is strongest when intent is explicit: Google branded search is still at 5.68% CTR and $0.21 CPC, materially cleaner than competitor search at $0.59 CPC.
The June 19 Whatagraph export succeeded, but trusted Meta, Google, Facebook, and Instagram data still stop at 2026-05-12. This is not a real June 13-19 performance read.
The frozen pizza category is large but soft: Circana data cited this week put U.S. frozen pizza at $7.3B, down 1.9% for the 52 weeks ended April 19, 2026.

Competitive pressure is moving in three directions at once: premium/process claims from Connie's, Di Fara, Zuppardi's and Pur Pain; private-label/co-op scale from Topco/AWG/Wakefern; and cleaner national-brand baselines as Nestle says it has removed artificial FD&C colors from its U.S. portfolio.

Price sensitivity is not theoretical: RELEX/Progressive Grocer reported 61% of shoppers changed food purchase volume because of higher prices, 47% switched to private label, and 51% stock up during promotions.
REPORTING: Fix the Whatagraph freshness issue before the next weekly read; leadership should not make June optimization calls from a May 12 cutoff.

PAID + CREATIVE: Keep Wisconsin origin and founder/process proof as controls, then add sharper value proof: why Real Dough is worth trading up for versus private label or promotion-driven alternatives.
SEARCH: Keep branded and sourdough-intent traffic protected; cap competitor search unless downstream conversion data proves it can justify the higher CPC.

AGENCY BRIEF: Build the next creative batch around fermentation proof, ingredient reassurance, retailer availability, and fast family-dinner utility. Avoid generic 'premium' language without a concrete shelf reason to believe.
DATA COVERAGE: Stand up a usable Real Dough review feed and current operations snapshot so customer voice and retail execution are not blind spots.

agency_brief.what_worked: Specific beats broad. The strongest available signals are Wisconsin-rooted ads, founder/operator education, sourdough/process credibility, ingredient reassurance, branded search, and practical store/dinner utility.
agency_brief.what_didnt: Generic premium positioning is not enough, competitor search remains the expensive paid pocket, and stale reporting makes week-over-week performance claims unsafe.
agency_brief.recommendation: Keep the creative system tight: Wisconsin origin, authentic sourdough fermentation, founder credibility, recognizable ingredients, and easy dinner value. Add one explicit value-defense lane that explains why the product is worth the premium when shoppers are trading down or waiting for promotions.
agency_brief.competitive_context: This week reinforced that the freezer set is getting more disciplined. The category is down 1.9% despite $7.3B in sales, scaled players are improving clean-label baselines, co-op/private-label programs are getting more capable, and restaurant-derived or process-forward brands are pushing format-specific claims. Real Dough should defend a narrower moat: real sourdough craft, Wisconsin credibility, clean ingredient proof, and retailer-ready velocity.

missing: No usable Real Dough review/sentiment feed. data/reviews.json still contains place-not-found errors for other MSHG brands, not Real Dough customer feedback.
No current-week Real Dough operations data. data/operations/ contains older Merriment snapshots from March/April, not Real Dough retail or operating inputs.
stale: The trusted Whatagraph analytics period remains 2026-01-01 through 2026-05-12, despite the June 19 export succeeding.
Week-over-week paid, Instagram, and Facebook top-line movement cannot be inferred because the source reporting window did not advance.
anomalies: YouTube and TikTok tabs in the Whatagraph export remain sample/demo data and are excluded from recommendations.
Facebook reel rows show 0 unique views while reporting average view time; use those rows only as directional content-theme evidence.
